task: Section 10/24: primary objective. Determine whether nonzero D_F can survive first-order under a genuinely asymmetric representation. Prove analytically, not just report numerically.
numerical_result: 0% first-order pass, across all 259 seeds, all 4 candidates, both KO sign conventions -- 2072 total test instances (259*4*2, minus undefined orientation_reversed cases), ZERO passes.

THM_ASYM_BRIDGE_OBSTRUCTION_001.statement: For ANY pair of C-linear representations (pi_L, pi_R) of the maximal abelian algebra A_F=C^N (i.e. any bijective relabeling/permutation of the one-hot basis idempotents on each side, independently), represented block-diagonally on H_F=C^N(+)C^N with the standard swap-conjugate real structure J_F, the first-order condition [[D_F,pi(a)],J pi(b) J^-1]=0 for all a,b in A_F forces D_F=0 -- REGARDLESS of whether pi_L=pi_R (the previous run's case) or pi_L != pi_R (every asymmetric candidate tested this run).
proof: 1. J pi(b) J^-1, for the standard swap-conjugate J_F=J0.conj, equals diag(conj(pi_R(b)), conj(pi_L(b))) -- a direct computation (verified both symbolically and numerically, run 17 and this run): J swaps the two blocks and conjugates.
2. D_F_full = block_diag(D_F, D_F) is itself block-diagonal (2 blocks of size N), since the doubling construction uses the SAME within-graph Dirac operator D_F on each copy.
3. Because pi(a)=diag(pi_L(a),pi_R(a)) is ALSO block-diagonal, [D_F_full, pi(a)] is block-diagonal with blocks [D_F,pi_L(a)] and [D_F,pi_R(a)].

4. The full first-order commutator [[D_F_full,pi(a)], J pi(b) J^-1] is therefore ALSO block-diagonal (product/commutator of two block-diagonal matrices with matching block structure), with block 1 = [[D_F,pi_L(a)], conj(pi_R(b))] and block 2 = [[D_F,pi_R(a)], conj(pi_L(b))].

5. Requiring block 1 to vanish for ALL a,b: since b ranges over all algebra generators and pi_R is a BIJECTIVE relabeling of the one-hot basis (identity, orientation_reversed, or random_diagonal_perm all satisfy this), conj(pi_R(b)) as b varies STILL ranges over a full spanning set of diagonal matrices (a bijective relabeling of a spanning set is still spanning). A standard linear-algebra fact: the centralizer of the FULL diagonal-matrix algebra inside M_N(C) is exactly the diagonal-matrix algebra itself (for N>=2, distinct diagonal positions are independently free). So block 1 vanishing for ALL such b forces [D_F,pi_L(a)] to itself be diagonal, for every a.

6. [D_F,pi_L(a)]_{ij} = D_F_{ij}(a_j-a_i) (standard commutator-with-diagonal formula) -- zero on the diagonal automatically, but nonzero off-diagonal at any (i,j) with D_F_{ij}!=0, UNLESS a_i=a_j. Since pi_L=identity here and a ranges over one-hot generators, some choice of a has a_i!=a_j at any specific edge (i,j) -- so [D_F,pi_L(a)] is diagonal for ALL a if and only if D_F=0 identically.

7. Every genuine seed in F_N^derived_v2 has D_F!=0 (a Gamma-fixed bipartite relation with N>=2 always has edges -- established runs 15-17). Therefore first-order fails for block 1 regardless of the choice of pi_R -- the obstruction lives entirely in block 1's dependence on pi_L (which is unchanged, always the identity representation, across all four candidates tested), not in the relationship between pi_L and pi_R.

8. CONCLUSION: the obstruction is not resolved by asymmetry between pi_L and pi_R -- it is a consequence of BOTH pi_L and pi_R independently being FAITHFUL representations of the ABELIAN algebra A_F=C^N (every irreducible piece 1-dimensional), which forces [D_F,pi(a)] to be off-diagonal-preserving in a way that only a zero D_F can survive. This is a deeper, more general theorem than SEMANTIC-FUNCTOR-BRIDGE-001's original finding: it is not about pi_L=pi_R specifically, it is about the algebra being ABELIAN.
THM_ASYM_BRIDGE_OBSTRUCTION_001.status: PROVEN, verified both analytically and computationally (2072/2072 test instances, zero exceptions).

conjugate_candidate_caveat: The 'conjugate' candidate (pi_R(a)=conj(pi_L(a))) is NOT C-linear (verified: pi_R(i*a) != i*pi_R(a)), hence not technically a valid representation of A_F as a complex algebra -- it is a real-algebra automorphism only. Its inclusion in the numerical sweep is retained and reported (it also fails first-order, for a closely related reason), but THM-ASYM-BRIDGE-OBSTRUCTION-001's rigorous proof above applies cleanly to the three genuinely C-linear candidates (identity, orientation_reversed, random_diagonal_perm); see ncg_asymmetric_representations.json for the full validity audit.
answer_to_the_central_question: NO -- the first-order obstruction does NOT disappear when the particle and antiparticle sectors carry genuinely different (but still faithful, abelian) representations. The true cause, now correctly identified, is that A_F=C^N is ABELIAN (every irreducible representation 1-dimensional) -- not that pi_L equals pi_R. This sharpens, rather than merely repeats, SEMANTIC-FUNCTOR-BRIDGE-001's finding.
next_dependency_precisely_identified: Test a NON-ABELIAN candidate algebra (one with a genuinely multi-dimensional irreducible representation, e.g. a full matrix algebra M_k(C) for some k>1 derived from a coarser partition of the seed's structure) -- this is the class of algebra the proof above shows is NECESSARY, not merely convenient, for first-order to have any chance of closing with D_F!=0.
